title: How can we use the MOJA Platform in Tanzania?
summary: An introduction to MOJA as a space for African adult and non-formal education practitioners to share knowledge, tell stories and build professional connections.

author.name: Joseph Masonda
author.role: Communications Officer | Digital Marketer | Website Designer | Content Creator | AI Enthusiast | Framer Developer | Writer

content.text: With an overwhelming amount of content scattered across the internet for learning, inspiration and information, it is easy to find yourself endlessly searching through links. In Adult and Non-Formal Education (ANFE), the challenge becomes even greater because different ministries, organisations and policies are involved across Africa.
Each country and organisation has its own programmes and initiatives, making it difficult for practitioners to find relevant information quickly in one place.

Across Africa, many organisations are implementing promising initiatives that promote non-formal education and community development, including skills-building programmes designed to create lasting change. For programme officers, communications experts, facilitators and educators, finding useful resources and people working on similar programmes can be time-consuming and frustrating.
MOJA provides a digital platform where practitioners can share and access knowledge, connect with colleagues and reach adult educators across Africa who are dealing with similar challenges.

The MOJA Community allows members to create profiles for themselves and their organisations, share insights, connect with others, and raise the visibility of activities and events. This can support more impactful work and stronger community development.

Launched in 2021, MOJA is Africa’s first and only digital platform focused on Adult Learning and Education (ALE) and ANFE. It has expanded to serve the continent. In Tanzania, it has already become a useful space for stakeholders to share best practices, learn from one another and network.

MOJA is user-generated: the more practitioners contribute, the more useful it becomes. During a workshop organised by DVV International on 3 September in Dar es Salaam, communications personnel, programme officers, IT experts and ALE practitioners explored how to use MOJA for advocacy and knowledge-sharing within their organisations.

One concern raised during the workshop was: what if I am not a skilled writer? Participants were sometimes afraid to share stories because they did not feel confident in writing. The workshop covered the basics of structuring stories, writing for impact, conducting research and applying ethical practices. Participants learned how to craft stories that resonate while discussing their storytelling challenges.

The hands-on session helped participants gain confidence to share their work. The MOJA Communications Handbook also provides practical guidance for writing articles and raising the visibility of activities and organisations.

Representatives from the Institute of Adult Education, Tanzania Education Network, University of Dar es Salaam, UNESCO and Tanganyika Christian Refugee Services attended. After the workshop, they selected topics related to their initiatives and agreed to share drafts in a dedicated WhatsApp group for peer review before uploading them to MOJA.

The WhatsApp group includes communications personnel from various organisations, the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology, the President’s Office – Regional Administration and Local Government, and ALE practitioners. It serves as a space for advocacy, networking and collaborative learning.

The journey to promote MOJA and related initiatives has been exciting and challenging. The goal is clear: advocate for the work being done in ALE and NFE in Tanzania and across Africa, helping initiatives reach wider audiences for exchange, learning and lasting impact.
Through platforms such as MOJA, people can connect, learn and inspire change through the networks, knowledge and partnerships they build.

Are you or your organisation part of the MOJA platform yet? Do you have a story to share or a resource to contribute? The invitation is open to join, connect and help grow this tool for the ALE community.
